title: 2000 Plus
paragraphs: A pioneering adult science-fiction anthology built around original stories of future technology, space travel, scientific experiments, and the consequences of invention.

Mutual science-fiction anthology created by Sherman H. Dreyer and produced with Robert Weenolsen. Contemporary/reference sources disagree on exact total episode count; frozen GRH subset contains seventeen files representing sixteen historical programs, including one alternate AFRS manifestation.
GRH documents the program through Mutual run (1950-03 to 1952-01) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Sherman H. Dreyer (creator (performer on 15 recordings), producer) (performer on 15 recordings), Robert Weenolsen (producer on 14 recordings), Elliot Jacoby (composer on 11 recordings and conductor on 2 recordings), Emerson Buckley (conductor on 10 recordings and composer on 1 recording), Walt Shaver (sound on 10 recordings, performer on 6 recordings, and sound-effects artist on 1 recording), and Ken Marvin (announcer on 10 recordings).
The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]] (broadcast on network).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include science fiction and speculative futures, future technology and technological anxiety, space travel and extraterrestrial exploration, aliens and extraterrestrial contact, robots, machines and automation, and AFRS rebroadcast preservation.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Early adult science-fiction radio anthology boom, Fragmentary 2000 Plus survival record, Korean War opening context for A Veteran Comes Home, and Postwar technological and Cold War context.

Programs with especially strong personnel connections in the GRH knowledge graph include [[show|x-minus-one|X Minus One]] (14 shared credited people), [[show|the-mysterious-traveler|The Mysterious Traveler]] (12 shared credited people), [[show|theater-five|Theater Five]] (11 shared credited people), [[show|words-at-war|Words at War]] (10 shared credited people), and [[show|cbs-radio-mystery-theater|CBS Radio Mystery Theater]] (9 shared credited people).
